title: Custom Sort Priority with CASE in ORDER BY
description:
Return all orders sorted by a **custom priority**: `'pending'` orders first, then `'completed'`, then anything else. Within each status group, sort by `total_amount` descending.

**Table: orders** — `id`, `customer_id`, `order_date`, `status`, `total_amount`

Output columns: `id`, `status`, `total_amount`. Order by custom priority then `total_amount` descending.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, order_date DATE, status VARCHAR, total_amount DECIMAL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,DATE '2026-01-05','completed',100.00),(2,2,DATE '2026-01-06','pending',300.00),(3,3,DATE '2026-01-07','pending',150.00),(4,4,DATE '2026-01-08','cancelled',80.00),(5,5,DATE '2026-01-09','completed',200.00);
solution_sql: SELECT id, status, total_amount FROM orders ORDER BY CASE status WHEN 'pending' THEN 1 WHEN 'completed' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END, total_amount DESC

test_cases.description: Pending (300, 150) first, then completed (200, 100), then cancelled (80)

hints: You can use a CASE expression directly inside ORDER BY.
The CASE maps each status to a sort number (1, 2, 3).
explanation: CASE in ORDER BY translates status values to priority numbers. Pending → 1 sorts first; completed → 2 second; everything else → 3 last. Within each group, ORDER BY total_amount DESC further sorts by amount.
